The method employs a 3D T2-weighted TSE sequence with a 1.5 mm isotropic resolution and a 10-minute scan duration, utilizing a 16-shot 4D motion correction algorithm. This algorithm sorts raw k-space data into 16 individual volumes based on respiratory phase, applies motion correction to each volume, and reconstructs a high-quality 3D reference image. The resulting 4D dataset comprises 16 motion-corrected 3D volumes corresponding to distinct respiratory phases, which are registered to the reference image to generate a 4D T2-weighted MRI. Validation was conducted on 10 healthy volunteers, comparing the proposed method against a standard 4D T2-weighted TSE sequence acquired with 160 breath-holds across 16 respiratory phases. Results demonstrated that the free-breathing approach yielded comparable image quality and geometric accuracy to the multi-breath-hold method, while significantly reducing scan time by a factor of 16. Consequently, this free-breathing motion-corrected 4D T2-weighted TSE MRI method offers a more efficient alternative for capturing high-quality 4D T2-weighted data in a single session.

This paper introduces a control synthesis method for ensuring Input Constrained Control Barrier Functions (ICCBFs) within nonlinear systems subject to closed-loop inputs. The proposed approach guarantees that system trajectories remain inside a specified safe set by synthesizing a control input that satisfies both safety and controllability requirements. The resulting control law is proven to be unique and computationally efficient, as it involves only the solution of a quadratic program. Furthermore, the method is extended to handle multiple coupled safety sets, and its efficacy is demonstrated through a numerical example.

This study introduces a novel approach to represent regions using CF-approximation spaces, which are defined by a pair of distinct, non-necessarily commuting mappings. Within this framework, the paper examines fundamental properties of CF-approximation spaces, including those related to CF-interiors, CF-closures, and CF-open sets. Furthermore, it analyzes the properties of CF-regular open sets and CF-regular closed sets, along with the definitions of CF-regularization and CF-irregularization operators. Finally, the authors explore the connections between CF-irregular approximation spaces and regular regions.

Paired-permutation testing is a nonparametric method used to evaluate the statistical significance of structured test values in paired data. This approach involves calculating the test statistic on the original dataset, then determining its frequency among the statistics derived from all possible paired sign inversions. While effective, the procedure becomes computationally prohibitive when dealing with high-dimensional data or complex test statistics that lack simple closed forms. To address this, we introduce a precise approximation for the paired-permutation distribution that relies on a specific subset of sign configurations. This new method is demonstrated to be highly efficient, particularly when the number of data pairs is large, and its validity is supported by rigorous theoretical analysis. We further illustrate its application and performance through various examples.

This paper introduces a comprehensive dataset covering the global container shipping industry from 1966 to 2019, encompassing freight rates, cargo volumes, prices for new and secondhand vessels, as well as scrapping costs. The authors detail the construction of this unified database, which integrates information from diverse sources and addresses inconsistencies in historical records. They further analyze the dataset's characteristics, highlighting the cyclical nature of the sector and the distinct volatility observed in newbuilding and scrapping prices compared to other market variables. Finally, the authors examine the long-term drivers of freight rates and cargo volumes, concluding that the expansion of global trade and the growth of world GDP are the primary determinants of these trends.

This paper presents a method to construct a veering triangulation for any pseudo-Anosov monodromy associated with a negative loom area. These triangulations serve as essential tools in analyzing pseudo-Anosov braids and their linked surface knots.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a dominant approach for addressing graph-structured data tasks, yet their reliance on fully connected layers often results in excessive parameter counts, leading to significant memory consumption and computational overhead. To address this, we introduce a novel GNN architecture that employs sparse connectivity to learn the graph's adjacency matrix directly from data. By integrating a sparse connectivity module with a sparse graph convolution layer, our method simultaneously learns both graph representations and the graph topology itself. Experimental evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining high efficiency.

Streaming matrix computations are essential for addressing large-scale machine learning challenges, with CountSketch serving as a foundational technique for these operations. This study investigates the robustness of CountSketch against adaptive inputs, specifically focusing on the scenario where an adversary constructs data to maximize the error of the algorithm. We demonstrate that, regardless of the adversary's strategy, CountSketch maintains a constant approximation ratio for the top-$k$ singular value decomposition (SVD). This holds true even when the adversary has complete knowledge of the CountSketch mechanism and can dynamically adjust the input matrix based on previous outputs. Our proof relies on a novel analysis of the adaptive adversary's limitations, revealing that their ability to create a significant discrepancy between the true and estimated singular values is inherently restricted.

This paper continues the investigation initiated in Part I, which examined the structure of complete manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature splittings. In this work, we demonstrate that any singularities within the splitting's singular set can be removed via a scalar curvature conformal transformation, thereby yielding a smooth manifold equipped with a totally geodesic scalar curvature flat splitting. This result serves as a foundational step toward characterizing the global structure of such manifolds.

The thermoelectric response of a superfluid subjected to a temperature gradient, known as the Nernst effect, serves as a sensitive probe for the presence of vortices and their dynamics. This study examines the linear response of a two-dimensional vortex liquid to a temperature gradient perpendicular to the vortex alignment. We derive the complete set of transport coefficients, including the transverse superfluid velocity and entropy currents, as well as the transverse heat and entropy conductivities. Our analysis reveals that the transverse Nernst coefficient is directly proportional to the transverse viscosity of the vortex liquid. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transverse entropy conductivity is governed by the mobility of the transverse entropy current.

This paper introduces a novel predictive control framework designed to enhance learning-based control by leveraging aggregate flexibility for real-time adjustments. While existing methods often rely on learning from historical data to generate control policies, this approach instead utilizes the inherent ability of flexible agents to adapt in real time to improve system performance. Specifically, it employs a rolling-horizon strategy that dynamically determines the necessary level of aggregate flexibility to satisfy future learning objectives. The proposed method is validated through a case study of a data center cooling system, demonstrating significant improvements in both energy efficiency and learning performance compared to conventional techniques.

This study introduces a novel hybrid framework combining BERT and GAN to forecast stock prices. The proposed method utilizes a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model to forecast the subsequent stock price based on the current price and its historical trend. Subsequently, a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) is employed to forecast the next day's stock price using the BERT output and historical data. The model is evaluated on the S&P 500 dataset, demonstrating that this BERT-GAN approach outperforms standalone BERT, LSTM, and CGAN models in terms of prediction accuracy.

The study of envelope modes in astrophysical systems has a long history, yet the lack of a unified formalism has hindered progress. This work introduces a new universal framework for envelope modes that encompasses both the traditional approximation and the anelastic approximation. This formalism is derived by applying a perturbation approach to the full linearized equations, utilizing the fact that in stellar envelopes, pressure dominates the total energy density. The resulting perturbation equations are significantly simpler than the original equations, allowing for the derivation of a WKB-like solution. This solution is expressed as a superposition of two components: a rapidly varying term and a slowly varying term. The latter is defined by a new quantity called the scattering matrix, which encapsulates the influence of the envelope on the wave modes. The validity of this approach is confirmed through comparisons with the traditional approximation, the anelastic approximation, and numerical simulations.

We examine the double Higgs boson production process in future 100 TeV electron-positron colliders, utilizing the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) framework to investigate potential Beyond Standard Model (BSM) interactions. Our analysis incorporates both the Standard Model Higgs sector and the heavy scalar sector of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM). We calculate the cross-sections for $e^+e^-\to ZHH$ and $e^+e^-\to \gamma HH$ scattering events, where the Higgs bosons decay into two bottom quark pairs ($HH\to b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$). By analyzing the kinematic distributions of the final state particles, we determine the sensitivity of these processes to BSM physics. Our findings indicate that the $e^+e^-\to ZHH$ channel offers superior sensitivity compared to the $e^+e^-\to \gamma HH$ channel. Furthermore, the $e^+e^-\to ZHH$ process is capable of probing the Higgs trilinear self-coupling ($\lambda_{HHH}$) with a precision of approximately 10%, while the quartic self-coupling ($\lambda_{HHZZ}$) can be investigated with a sensitivity of roughly 10%.

Although the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity are mathematically equivalent to those of scalar-tensor theories, a direct correspondence between their specific Lagrangian forms has remained elusive. This study establishes a precise mapping between the Lagrangian of $f(R)$ gravity and that of scalar-tensor theory. By applying a specific transformation to the metric within the $f(R)$ framework, we derive an auxiliary metric that renders the action explicitly equivalent to the scalar-tensor form. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this constructed action remains invariant under conformal transformations.

We present a novel computational framework for analyzing collisions of localized shocks in AdS$_5$, which are characterized by a transverse profile and depend solely on longitudinal coordinates and time. This method is built upon a series expansion in lateral gradients, with its leading order term derived from a holographic generalization of the Bjorken flow. By employing this approach, we calculate the evolution of the energy density and shear stress for a collision of two Gaussian-shaped shocks in AdS$_5$, demonstrating that the model accurately captures the initial dynamics and the subsequent formation of a quark-gluon plasma droplet.

This study examines the anisotropic drag acting on a long, slender cylinder moving through a fluid-filled granular bed. We derive a theoretical model for the drag force that incorporates the mechanical properties of the granular material, the fluid's characteristics, and the object's dimensions. Experimental results obtained from both glass beads and sand confirm the validity of this model. Furthermore, we observe that the critical velocity required to initiate fluidization is significantly higher for cylinders moving parallel to the grain flow compared to those moving perpendicularly.

We present spatially resolved observations of the [O III] 5007 Å emission line for the nearby (z = 0.011) disk galaxy SDSS J1030+0524, utilizing the Keck/DIMMOS integral field spectrograph. This galaxy exhibits a high star formation rate (SFR) of 100 M☉ yr⁻¹, a superwind velocity of 1,000 km s⁻¹, and a gas outflow rate of 100 M☉ yr⁻¹, which exceeds its star formation rate by a factor of 1.5. Our analysis reveals that the outflow is spatially confined to the central regions, specifically within the inner 10 kpc, where the specific star formation rate (SSFR) is 0.1 Gyr⁻¹. This confinement correlates with a high gas surface density (Σ_gas) of 100 M☉ pc⁻², which exceeds the critical threshold (Σ_crit) required for outflow generation. Consequently, we propose that the observed outflow is driven by a combination of supernovae and radiation pressure, which are most effective in the galaxy's high-density central regions.

We introduce BoGraph, a novel method for Bayesian optimization that automatically extracts and organizes historical data from system logs. This approach is specifically designed to address the challenge of optimizing complex systems with numerous parameters when historical data is abundant but current data collection is prohibitively expensive. BoGraph operates by first constructing a directed acyclic graph (DAG) from the raw logs, which captures the intricate dependencies among parameters and their interrelations with system outputs. Leveraging this structural DAG, BoGraph builds a scalable Bayesian optimization model that effectively utilizes historical data to inform and enhance the search for new optimal configurations. We evaluated BoGraph on both real-world and synthetic datasets, demonstrating that it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization techniques in terms of sample efficiency.

We present an analysis of elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV using the multiphase transport (AMPT) model. Our results indicate that AMPT accurately reproduces the measured $v_2$ and $v_3$ values for Au+Au systems, as well as the $v_2$ data for Cu+Cu collisions. However, the model fails to capture the $v_3$ data for Cu+Cu collisions, predicting a value that is significantly higher than experimental observations. We attribute this discrepancy to the AMPT model's inability to generate sufficient initial spatial anisotropy in Cu+Cu collisions, which is essential for driving the observed triangular flow.

The widespread adoption of Linked Data has driven a significant increase in the volume of RDF datasets available on the internet. However, the lack of rigorous quality control mechanisms has resulted in numerous RDF sources containing errors and inconsistencies. This paper introduces a novel framework designed to assess the quality of RDF datasets by integrating diverse evaluation methods. It addresses critical challenges inherent in processing large-scale RDF data, including efficient storage, parallel computation, and the management of distributed memory. Implemented using Apache Spark, the framework is evaluated through experiments on various RDF datasets, demonstrating its capability to handle datasets exceeding 100 GB in size.

This paper introduces a novel, robust, and efficient method for estimating the parameters of discretely observed stochastic processes. The approach relies on a robust estimator derived from the asymptotic quasi-likelihood framework, which remains valid regardless of the underlying distribution. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that these proposed estimators achieve asymptotic normality and efficiency. Furthermore, the study addresses the challenge of selecting a robust bandwidth parameter. The method's performance is validated through simulation experiments and an application to real-world data.

We present the first comprehensive analysis of emission-line ratios in the nuclear regions of 10 Seyfert galaxies, utilizing integral field spectroscopy from the VLT/KMOS instrument. Our study focuses on the ionization mechanism of the narrow-line region (NLR) by mapping the chemical composition of the interstellar medium (ISM) and comparing it against the established AGN ionization sequence. Our findings reveal that the chemical abundances of the NLR in these galaxies deviate significantly from the standard AGN ionization axis. Specifically, the NLRs are located far below the axis, indicating metal-enriched conditions relative to the trend. This enrichment is likely driven by the host galaxy's intense star formation activity, which drives the NLR abundances to align with the main sequence of star-forming galaxies. Furthermore, we observe a distinct correlation between the degree of chemical deviation from the axis and the Eddington ratio, suggesting that the extent of this offset is governed by the central engine's accretion rate. These results imply that the canonical AGN ionization axis is not a universal standard for NLR chemistry. Instead, the chemical signatures of the NLR appear to be heavily influenced by the host galaxy's evolutionary history and its current star formation rates.

This paper introduces a novel event-driven evaluation framework designed for edge computing environments. This framework enables the dynamic assessment of edge applications by leveraging the inherent characteristics of data events. It incorporates a new event-driven function language and an associated type system to support the specification of application logic. Furthermore, it provides a static analysis method to verify the type safety of event-driven functions. The utility and effectiveness of this framework are demonstrated through a prototype implementation and practical case studies.

The ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider has conducted extensive investigations into the mixing, CP violation, and rare decays of beauty mesons. This presentation outlines the experimental findings from ATLAS regarding these phenomena, with a specific focus on the decay modes $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to K^{*0}\mu^+\mu^-$.

Traffic simulation is essential for developing and evaluating autonomous driving technologies, yet current methods often struggle to generate lifelike traffic scenarios. This paper introduces a new framework called SceneGen, which leverages a deep generative model to synthesize realistic traffic scenes. SceneGen operates by learning the underlying distribution of traffic elements from real-world data, enabling it to produce diverse and plausible configurations. Specifically, the model learns to generate traffic participants—such as cars and pedestrians—along with their attributes, including positions, velocities, and dimensions. Additionally, it creates corresponding road layouts that align with these elements. Experiments demonstrate that SceneGen successfully captures the complex correlations among traffic components and their relationship with the surrounding environment.
This study investigates the Ising model within a Cayley tree framework, demonstrating the existence of new weakly periodic Gibbs states characterized by a minimal period of four.

This study introduces a preconditioning framework for the linear systems encountered within structure-preserving discretizations of partial differential equations, specifically targeting the preservation of discrete invariants such as Casimir functions and momentum maps. The proposed approach relies on a discrete Poisson structure that is isomorphic to a constant-coefficient Poisson structure, enabling the use of standard preconditioned Krylov subspace methods while maintaining the preservation of the original discrete invariants. The text demonstrates the method's efficacy through applications to the Euler equations on a Lie group and the Euler–Poincaré equations on a Lie algebra, with results indicating that the proposed scheme retains discrete invariants and achieves a convergence rate of first order.

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a standard probability space, and let $T: X \to X$ be a measure-preserving transformation that is ergodic and non-periodic. We demonstrate that for any ergodic, non-periodic sequence $(f_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of such transformations, the joint process $(f_n(x), f_n(y))$ is ergodic and non-periodic with respect to the product measure $\mu \times \mu$ on $X \times X$, provided that $T$ is ergodic and non-periodic. As a consequence, we derive several new findings regarding the ergodicity of sequences of functions.

We investigate the formation of dust particles in low-metallicity environments, specifically focusing on the transition from molecular clouds to supernova remnants. Our study examines how dust growth and the subsequent evolution of dusty environments are influenced by variations in metallicity and the ambient gas density. We find that dust particles can grow to sizes of approximately 0.1 micrometers within molecular clouds, even at metallicity levels as low as 0.01 times solar. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the presence of dust significantly alters the thermal and dynamical properties of these clouds. Specifically, the cooling timescales of low-metallicity molecular clouds are reduced by a factor of roughly 10 due to dust emission. Additionally, the presence of dust increases the Jeans mass by a factor of 100, thereby suppressing the formation of stars in these regions. Finally, we explore the impact of supernovae on the dusty interstellar medium, concluding that the resulting shock waves can effectively destroy dust particles in low-metallicity settings.

This paper introduces Far3Det, a novel framework designed for far-field 3D identification. Addressing the scarcity of existing datasets that support both 3D user modeling and far-zone data capture, we present Far3D, a new dataset comprising 100 three-dimensional human avatars and 10,000 corresponding far-field acoustic measurements. Within our proposed Far3Det architecture, we integrate a 3D human encoder with a transformer-based decoder to facilitate 3D-driven far-field acoustic scene generation. Furthermore, we introduce a 3D-aware cross-attention mechanism to enhance the fusion of 3D structural information with acoustic inputs. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that Far3Det achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D user identification tasks using far-field acoustic data.

Quantum machine learning (QML) has recently emerged as a promising avenue for addressing challenges in condensed matter physics, particularly within the realm of quantum many-body systems. This study introduces a novel variational quantum algorithm designed to generate approximate ground states of spin chains and Heisenberg antiferromagnets. By employing a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) with trainable parameters, the method optimizes these values to minimize the expectation value of the system's Hamiltonian. Crucially, the proposed approach incorporates a specific ansatz that integrates a quantum neural network (QNN) with a quantum Fourier transform (QFT) layer. This hybrid architecture enables the model to learn from data and generalize effectively, thereby reducing the number of required variational iterations. Furthermore, the algorithm demonstrates robustness against noise, maintaining performance even when executed on a simulated noisy environment. Numerical simulations indicate that this method successfully generates ground states for spin chains and Heisenberg antiferromagners across various lattice sizes, with the QFT component facilitating faster convergence.

We introduce a novel framework for aligning non-rigid volumes to surfaces by integrating biomechanical priors with data-driven deep learning. This approach models the deformation field as a linear combination of basis modes derived from a biomechanical simulation, where the coefficients are predicted by a neural network. Experiments on the MICCAI 2019 segmentation challenge dataset demonstrate that this method achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing both traditional and recent deep learning-based techniques.

We demonstrate that the conformal Killing vectors associated with the energy-momentum tensor of a spherically symmetric, stationary spacetime are either trivial or correspond to the spacetime's isometries. This result is established by analyzing the specific form of the energy-momentum tensor for such spacetimes and applying the relevant conformal Killing equations.

Scene flow estimation is a critical task in autonomous driving, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent complexity of 3D motion and the limitations of 2D cameras. While recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved performance, these models typically require vast amounts of labeled data. To mitigate this data dependency, we introduce a novel approach for self-supervised flow learning that leverages unlabeled video sequences. Our method employs a metric learning framework to identify pairs of image patches with similar motion characteristics, explicitly training the network to distinguish similar instances from dissimilar ones. To achieve this, we propose an adversarial metric learning architecture that utilizes a discriminator to detect motion-inconsistent pairs. This discriminator is trained via a flow prediction module, which generates flow fields from pairs of images to capture motion information. Our experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques on both KITTI and Sintel benchmarks.

This study introduces a novel classification framework based on a Spiking Random Neural Network (RNN) that integrates a two-stage training methodology. Initially, a conventional feedforward neural network is trained using backpropagation to establish optimal weights and biases, which are subsequently mapped to the parameters of the spiking RNN. In the second phase, these initial RNN parameters undergo fine-tuning via a gradient-based algorithm specifically adapted for spiking neural networks. Experimental evaluations on the MNIST and EMNIST datasets demonstrate that this proposed RNN achieves a classification accuracy of 99.6% and 97.1%, respectively, while maintaining an energy consumption of merely 0.011 joules per image.

This study examines the impact of an external magnetic field on the structure of spin-polarized strange quark stars at finite temperature, utilizing the MIT bag model. By analyzing the thermodynamic properties of a spin-polarized quark gas under these conditions, we derive the equation of state and calculate the maximum mass supported by such a star. Our findings indicate that the presence of the magnetic field significantly alters the equation of state, resulting in a substantial increase in the star's maximum mass.

This paper investigates the relationship between the chromatic index of a cubic graph $G$, denoted $\chi'(G)$, and its ideal matching number, $\alpha_I(G)$. We establish that for any cubic graph $G$ containing a vertex $v$ with degree 3 such that $G - \{e\}$ has a Hamiltonian cycle for every edge $e$ incident to $v$, the inequality $\chi'(G) + \alpha_I(G) \le 7$ holds. Additionally, we identify a specific class of cubic graphs where $\chi'(G) + \alpha_I(G) = 6$.

We introduce the concept of a block arrangement, defined as a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ into disjoint blocks $B_1, B_2, \dots$ such that for any non-constant polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, the set of integers $k$ where $f(\mathbb{Z}^n) \cap B_k = \{k\}$ is infinite. This paper demonstrates that block arrangements exist in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for all $n \geq 1$. Additionally, we establish a generalization of Schur's theorem: for any $n \geq 1$ and polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, there exists a constant $C$ such that for every block arrangement with blocks $B_1, B_2, \dots$, there is an index $k$ where $f(\mathbb{Z}^n) \cap B_k$ contains at least $C$ distinct integers.

System calls serve as the primary interface for applications to interact with the operating system kernel, yet their implementation within the Linux kernel is often suboptimal. This inefficiency stems from the fact that system call policies are highly dependent on specific application behaviors, which are difficult to predict. While prior research has attempted to address this by automatically learning system call policies, those methods have largely been limited to monolithic applications. In this paper, we introduce Timeloops, a novel system call policy learning framework designed for containerized microservices. Timeloops leverages the inherent modularity of microservices to achieve scalability and employs a lightweight, application-agnostic approach to capture process behaviors. Furthermore, Timeloops incorporates a new learning algorithm that utilizes timing information to infer application behavior, enabling it to learn effective system call policies with minimal overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that Timeloops significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, delivering up to a 1.65x performance improvement for microservices.

This study examines the stability of the dark matter (DM) candidate within the $B-L$ augmented Standard Model, where the DM candidate is the pseudo-Goldstone boson (pGB) arising from the spontaneous breaking of a global $U(1)_{pGB}$ symmetry. In this framework, the pGB acquires mass through loop corrections involving $B-L$ gauge bosons, with its mass scale determined by the gauge coupling strength and the vacuum expectation value of the $B-L$ scalar field. We analyze the pGB's interactions with Standard Model particles, focusing on the annihilation processes that determine the relic density. Specifically, we investigate the impact of $B-L$ gauge boson loops on the annihilation cross-section into $W$ boson pairs, as well as the contributions from tree-level annihilations into fermion pairs. We further explore the parameter space compatible with observed DM abundance, considering both the $B-L$ gauge boson mass and the pGB mass. Our findings indicate that a pGB mass of approximately 100 GeV can satisfy cosmological constraints, provided the $B-L$ gauge boson mass is sufficiently large.

This work addresses the optimal filtering problem for a network of sensors tracking an unknown number of targets, where the origin of each target is represented by its probability density. We introduce a new origin model that integrates a grid-based approach with a non-parametric Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (NMHT) method. This hybrid model utilizes a grid structure for the prior probability of target origins, while the non-parametric MHT handles the posterior probability without relying on a grid. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this proposed origin model achieves a balance between high accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, these results indicate that the suggested method is particularly well-suited for sensor management applications.

This study investigates the null controllability of a population dynamics model featuring interior decay, expressed as a nonlinear hyperbolic PDE with source and sink terms. By applying Carleman estimates, we first establish an observability inequality for the corresponding homogeneous system. Subsequently, we derive the source term estimate required to prove the existence of an appropriate feedback control that drives the population to extinction within a finite timeframe.

Soccer players must execute appropriate actions to secure victories, yet their ability to do so is frequently hindered by the unpredictable nature of the sport. To address this challenge, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework designed to enhance player actions during critical game moments. Our approach utilizes a multi-agent system where each player is modeled as an autonomous agent. We define a reward function that incentivizes goal-scoring and penalizes conceding, thereby guiding the learning process. Through extensive training, our multi-agent DRL model achieves a win rate of 60% against a baseline of random actions in simulated matches.

This study introduces a novel inversion framework for extended sources in full-waveform inversion (FWI), specifically designed to enhance the time-domain acoustic wave equation method. Addressing the limitations of current approaches, which often rely on frequency-domain techniques or time-domain strategies that necessitate computationally expensive time-domain convolution, this paper proposes a new strategy utilizing a time-domain pseudo-spectral approach. This method incorporates a convolutional auxiliary equation to efficiently handle the source term, thereby eliminating the need for traditional convolution operations. The proposed scheme is validated through numerical experiments involving an extended source, demonstrating its efficacy in accurately reconstructing subsurface structures.

Optical anisotropy, a property where materials exhibit direction-dependent characteristics, is typically achieved through the alignment of molecular dipoles or the arrangement of atomic orbitals. This study demonstrates that quantum squeezing can generate anisotropy in an optically isotropic system. Specifically, we examine a two-dimensional array of atoms interacting with a single squeezed vacuum field. Our findings reveal that while the atomic ensemble remains in a pure state, its reduced density matrix displays anisotropic features. This induced anisotropy is characterized by a distinct "squeezing angle" and is further modulated by the detuning between the light and atomic resonance, as well as the strength of atom-atom interactions.

We report the findings of an analysis of data from the AstroSat mission regarding the X-ray source IGR J19294+1816, a low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB) that underwent a 2019 outburst. Utilizing observations from the Soft X-ray Telescope (SXT) and the Transition Region and Coronal Explorer (TRACER) instruments, we identified a broad spectral feature consistent with a cyclotron line at approximately 1.5 keV, alongside a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) in the mHz range with a period of roughly 600 seconds. The detection of this low-frequency QPO, combined with the presence of the cyclotron line, supports the classification of IGR J19294+1816 as an accretion disk instability (ADI) source. Furthermore, the observed spectral properties align with those of other known ADI sources, suggesting that the mHz QPO and cyclotron line are likely associated with the same physical mechanism.

We investigate the impact of environmental noise on species interactions within a two-species elector model featuring a competition-colonization tradeoff. In this framework, one species relies on competitive superiority, while the other utilizes competitive strategies. Our findings indicate that noise can either facilitate species coexistence or trigger the elimination of the colonizer, depending on the specific noise intensity. Furthermore, we demonstrate that noise-induced coexistence can persist even when deterministic conditions predict extinction.

Indonesian sundials, or *suryakala*, represent a significant historical legacy that has largely remained undocumented. This study aims to record sundials across Indonesia, with a specific focus on those bearing inscriptions. The research methodology involved a comprehensive literature review and a systematic field survey conducted between 2018 and 2020. The findings reveal that Indonesian sundials were primarily utilized for religious observance, particularly to determine prayer times. Furthermore, the study identifies that these instruments were crafted by Muslim communities, with the majority located in Java.

This study introduces a novel integrated data and energy networking (IDEN) framework designed to support D2D communications, specifically targeting the simultaneous transmission of information and energy to D2D receivers. Within this model, an energy-harvesting D2D pair is established, where the transmitter leverages a cognitive reflecting surface (IRS) to facilitate data transmission and energy delivery to an energy-harvesting D2D user. The primary objective is to maximize the harvested energy for the D2D receiver by optimizing the IRS phase shifts, the data transmission power, and the energy transmission power. To achieve this, a non-convex optimization problem is formulated, which is subsequently resolved via a low-complexity iterative algorithm. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed IDEN framework significantly enhances energy efficiency for D2D users compared to conventional data-only transmission methods.

This study details the remote deployment of a single-beam Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) setup to conduct two-dimensional structural testing. By utilizing two retroreflectors positioned at separate locations on the target structure, the system captures vibration data from both points simultaneously. The authors describe the configuration of the LDV apparatus, the associated data processing algorithms, and the experimental results. The findings demonstrate that this approach achieves a measurement distance of 1.5 meters with a spatial resolution of 0.01 mm and a velocity resolution of 0.01 mm/s.

This study introduces a novel programmable phase plate (PPP) designed to dynamically adjust the electron wave's phase, thereby enabling active aberration correction in a Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM). The PPP consists of a silicon nitride membrane embedded with a micro-fabricated array of silicon pillars, where the height of each pillar is precisely controlled to modify the local phase shift. By adjusting pillar heights, the device can compensate for spherical aberration ($C_s$) and defocus ($\Delta z$). Theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm that the PPP can correct $C_s$ and $\Delta z$ with a resolution of 1 nm and 0.1 nm, respectively. Furthermore, the system demonstrates the capability to correct astigmatism with a 0.1 nm limit. Consequently, this PPP functions as a versatile programmable aberration corrector, offering a cost-effective solution for TEMs lacking such hardware.

Recent advancements in dialogue systems have largely relied on neural networks, specifically encoder-decoder architectures, to generate responses. However, these models often lack transparency, making it difficult to understand the information encoded within their internal representations. This study investigates whether such latent representations contain task-relevant details by introducing a novel task-oriented information metric. This metric is derived from the mutual information between the task input and the encoder's output representations. Experiments conducted on the MultiWOZ dataset reveal that the proposed measure effectively captures task-related information. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the task input and encoder representations share a significant amount of mutual information, indicating that these latent states do indeed convey meaningful task-specific data.

This study introduces a novel attention-based deep learning network designed for place recognition using 3D LiDAR data. The proposed architecture incorporates a multi-scale feature extraction module alongside a novel attention mechanism to enhance the network's ability to capture discriminative features. Furthermore, the network integrates a multi-task learning strategy that jointly optimizes feature extraction and classification tasks. Experimental evaluations conducted on the KITTI and nuScenes datasets demonstrate that AttDLNet achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Streaming video transcoding is a computationally demanding process that relies heavily on cloud infrastructure. This study evaluates the performance of transcoding services offered by major cloud providers, specifically Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (Google Cloud). The evaluation methodology involves measuring the processing times for various video resolutions and bitrates across both services. The results indicate that Google Cloud consistently outperforms AWS, delivering a 1.5 to 2.5 times faster processing speed. Furthermore, the study develops a queuing model to characterize the performance behavior of these cloud services.

This study investigates the temperature-dependent behavior of the heat capacity and the Kohn anomaly in doped graphene sheets. By calculating the electronic heat capacity via the density of states (DOS) and the lattice heat capacity using the Debye model, we determined the total heat capacity. Our findings indicate that the Kohn anomaly significantly influences the heat capacity of doped graphene, with its magnitude varying according to the doping level.

Speech production is a complex process where individuals generate utterances based on their internal intentions and the surrounding context. While masking strategies have been identified as a critical mechanism in speech production, existing research has primarily focused on isolated words or sentences, overlooking the broader contextual environment. This study introduces a novel experimental setup designed to investigate masking strategies within a more comprehensive context. The results indicate that masking effects are robustly observed in this expanded context, demonstrating that individuals tend to omit specific phonetic details when generating speech. Furthermore, the research reveals that these effects are significantly influenced by the contextual surroundings, suggesting that masking is not merely a local phenomenon but is highly sensitive to context. These findings offer new insights into the mechanisms of human speech production.

This paper examines the spectral and orbital stability properties of solitary wave solutions to the Klein–Gordon equation coupled with an anharmonic oscillator. We establish the linearized operator's spectral characteristics and utilize these findings to determine the conditions under which solitary waves exhibit orbital stability.

We investigate the stability of Q-balls carrying multiple discrete charges, which arise when scalar fields possess multiple charge couplings. We demonstrate that these multi-charged Q-balls can exhibit stability even if the corresponding single-charge Q-balls are unstable. Furthermore, we identify configurations with multiple cores, which are found to be energetically favorable compared to single-core counterparts.

This study examines cyclic cosmology incorporating holographic dark matter, utilizing the future event horizon to define the cutoff scale. By analyzing the holographic dark matter density within this cyclic framework, we demonstrate that the matter density remains consistent with current observational data throughout the cyclic era. Furthermore, we establish that the cyclic model aligns with the holographic principle, as the total energy density adheres to holographic constraints. Finally, we derive the equation of state for holographic dark matter within the cyclic setting and determine the conditions required for the universe to undergo recollapse.

This study examines the relationship between the Hermitian matrix of a directed graph and its scattering matrix. We establish that the eigenvalues of the Hermitian matrix correspond to the eigenvalues of the scattering matrix, which are determined by the eigenvalues of the directed adjacency matrix. Furthermore, we derive a formula for the multiplicity of any specific eigenvalue of the Hermitian matrix. Finally, we introduce a novel formula for the characteristic polynomial of the Hermitian matrix.

This paper establishes a non-commutative extension of Leopoldt's theorem applicable to $\mathbb{Q}$, covering both p-adic and classical scenarios. Specifically, we examine the p-adic independence of characters within the Galois group of Q, demonstrating that these characters are independent if and only if their associated p-adic Hodge-Tate weights are distinct. Additionally, we derive a non-commutative formulation of the classical theorem by proving that the Galois group of Q, when acting on characters with distinct p-adic Hodge-Tate weights, is torsion-free.

We investigate the potential of Belle II to detect axion-like particles (ALPs) originating from $B$ meson decays, considering both ALPs that remain visible in the detector and those that are dislocated. For visible ALPs, we establish Belle II's sensitivity to the ALP-nucleon coupling ($g_{aN}$) and ALP-photon coupling ($g_{a\gamma}$) across a mass spectrum from 1 to 10 GeV. Additionally, we analyze the reach for dislocated ALPs, which decay into photon pairs within the electromagnetic calorimeter's acceptance region, finding that Belle II can probe $g_{a\gamma}$ values up to $10^{-3}$ for masses between 1 and 10 GeV.

This study investigates the efficacy of contextualized language models in identifying semantic modifications within news articles. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 10,000 pairs of news excerpts, where each pair features a single lexical alteration. Our findings indicate that contextualized language models substantially outperform traditional methods on this task, achieving a F1 score of 61.1%. Furthermore, we analyze the model's performance across various lexical categories, including proper nouns, verbs, and adjectives.

The formation of ultralight bosons through the superradiant instability of spinning compact objects serves as a compelling probe for physics beyond the Standard Model. While this mechanism has been extensively studied for rotating black holes, it also applies to spinning compact stars. This paper demonstrates that the interaction between superradiant ultralight bosons and the magnetic fields surrounding heavy quasars can generate distinctive observational signatures. Specifically, we analyze the impact of such fields on the boson's effective mass and the resulting energy spectrum emitted by the star. Our findings indicate that the presence of a strong magnetic field can significantly alter the radiated spectrum, potentially enabling the detection of ultralight bosons via the spectral features of spinning quasars.

Interkinetic nuclear migration (INM) is a cell division process where nuclei move along the apical-basal axis of a tissue. While the mechanisms driving INM are well understood in the developing vertebrate retina, the specific rules governing the movement of nuclei between division cycles remain unclear. This study proposes that INM in the zebrafish retina functions as a diffusive process, driven by the opposing effects of active transport toward the apical surface and basal surface. We demonstrate that this model accurately accounts for the observed nuclear trajectories and the distribution of nuclei within the tissue. Furthermore, we show that the diffusive framework can predict nuclear positioning during the cell cycle and the impact of pharmacological agents on INM dynamics.

This paper introduces a novel class of linear codes designed to facilitate source separation in video demosaicing and compressive video reconstruction. The proposed codes are derived from a specific construction of linear codes that satisfy a newly defined property termed the "color image demosaicing property" (CDP). We establish that these codes possess a minimum distance of at least three, which is sufficient to enable the recovery of missing color information. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed codes achieve a rate comparable to that of existing linear codes meeting the CDP. Numerical simulations confirm the efficacy of the proposed codes in both video demosaicing and compressive video recovery applications.

We examine incompressible polar active liquids containing quenched disorder, focusing on dimensions $d>2$. By applying a hydrodynamic framework, we derive a renormalized constitutive relation that incorporates the effects of disorder. Our analysis reveals that disorder induces a transition from a turbulent state to a polar-ordered phase, characterized by a discontinuous jump in the average polar order parameter. This transition is accompanied by a discontinuous change in the effective activity, which is found to be negative. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this transition is driven by a mechanism analogous to a first-order phase transition.

This study introduces a novel approach to analyzing the vulnerability of academic collaboration networks by integrating network dynamics with structural hole theory. The method models network evolution through the lens of network dynamics, utilizing a node addition and removal mechanism grounded in structural hole concepts to simulate network robustness. The proposed framework was applied to analyze the academic collaboration network of the United States, with results indicating that the network exhibits a high degree of robustness. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the network's vulnerability is primarily driven by the removal of nodes possessing a high degree and a significant number of structural holes.

The pseudogap phase of cuprate superconductors is characterized by a depletion of spectral weight near the Fermi level, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. This study proposes that the pseudogap arises from a Mott-like insulating state driven by strong electron-electron interactions, which becomes accessible due to an extraordinary enhancement of the van Hove singularity at specific doping levels. This enhancement results from a geometric reconstruction of the Fermi surface, which induces a vanishing effective mass and a logarithmic divergence in the electronic specific heat. This phenomenon is supported by a comprehensive analysis of experimental data, including specific heat, optical conductivity, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES).

This paper introduces a novel device designed to investigate spallation neutrons within the Aberdeen Tunnel laboratory. The apparatus consists of a 100 kV, 100 mA electrostatic linear accelerator, which directs a 100 MeV proton beam onto a tungsten target. This setup generates a neutron flux of 10^10 n/s, with a beam diameter of 10 cm and a divergence of 10 mrad. The device is capable of producing neutrons with energies ranging from 100 MeV down to 10 keV.

This paper investigates the existence of normalized ground states for a biharmonic Choquard equation subject to a potential exhibiting exponential essential growth, within the framework of Sobolev spaces. The approach relies on variational methods, specifically utilizing a minimax strategy grounded on a newly established compactness result for a category of Palais-Smale sequences.

The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) has recently completed its inaugural two-year mission, during which it conducted all-sky observations to identify thousands of exoplanet candidates. While the majority of these detections are small, low-mass planets orbiting M-dwarf stars, the data quality for these targets remains insufficient to determine their precise masses and assess the prevalence of terrestrial planets in the habitable zone. To address this limitation, the TESS-Keck Partnership has been established to utilize the Keck I and II telescopes for high-precision radial velocity measurements of the most promising TESS candidates. This initiative aims to characterize the smallest planets discovered by TESS, thereby advancing our comprehension of planetary system architectures and the conditions conducive to life. This paper outlines the selection criteria for the initial batch of targets and presents the anticipated outcomes of the study.

This study introduces an Indonesian Identity Card (KTP) data extraction system designed to automate the retrieval of personal information from digital images. The proposed method integrates Character-level Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Char-LSTM) networks with Conditional Random Fields (CRF) to enhance the accuracy of Indonesian language-based Character Recognition (OCR). The system was evaluated on a dataset comprising 100 KTP images, achieving a precision of 99%, recall of 99%, and an F1 score of 99%.

We present a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach to calculate the ground state wave function and its associated energy for a quantum harmonic oscillator subjected to constant external forces. By employing the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, we demonstrate that this method remains effective even when the system is driven by time-varying forces. Furthermore, we apply these techniques to analyze a damped, driven quantum harmonic oscillator with time-dependent parameters, utilizing the derived MCMC framework to generate data for the path integral method.

The YORP effect, resulting from the anisotropic absorption and reflection of solar radiation, causes a gradual change in an asteroid's spin rate. This phenomenon is most pronounced in smaller bodies, where the rotation velocity can increase or decrease over time. This study analyzes the YORP impact on three specific asteroids—(10115) 1992 SK, (1685) Toro, and (1620) Geographos—by utilizing their shape models and orbital data to calculate the magnitude of this effect.

Social media platforms have become the primary venues for political discourse, yet the mechanisms driving these interactions remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the network dynamics of political accounts on Instagram, analyzing how their connections influence the flow of information and the formation of public opinion. We constructed a directed network comprising 1,000 prominent political Instagram accounts and 1.5 million edges, where links represent mutual following relationships. Our analysis reveals that the network exhibits a hierarchical structure characterized by distinct communities and a core group of highly influential actors. Furthermore, we identified a strong positive correlation between a user's network centrality and their actual political reach, as measured by follower counts. Finally, we developed a novel metric to quantify the "political temperature" of the network, demonstrating that this metric effectively captures shifts in the collective political sentiment of Instagram users.

A subset $X$ within a metric space $(Z,d)$ is termed Roelcke precompact if every family of $Z$'s non-expansive mappings possesses a finite-dimensional net that is $\epsilon$-dense for any $\epsilon > 0$. This study demonstrates that the collection of homeomorphisms of a compact, simply connected Riemann surface which act as sense-preserving on the boundary fails to be Roelcke precompact.

Determining the physical properties of M dwarfs is essential for understanding their evolution and for characterizing the planets orbiting them. This study presents a new method for estimating the effective temperature ($T_{\rm eff}$), surface gravity ($\log g$), and metallicity ([Fe/H]) of M dwarfs by utilizing the spectral energy distribution (SED) derived from multi-wavelength photometry. We applied this technique to a sample of 100 field M dwarfs, utilizing spectral types and $T_{\rm eff}$ values from the literature to validate the results. The approach demonstrates strong agreement with existing data, yielding a mean absolute error of 100 K for $T_{\rm eff}$ and 0.05 dex for $\log g$. Furthermore, the derived stellar parameters were used to construct a new M-dwarf evolutionary track, which aligns well with the observed color-magnitude diagram (CMD) of the sample. Finally, we utilized these refined parameters to analyze the distribution of M dwarfs in the $T_{\rm eff}$–[Fe/H] plane, revealing a bimodal pattern in metallicity that mirrors findings for other stellar types.

Line ripples, which are dual metasurfaces composed of two distinct metallic strip patterns, have recently garnered significant attention due to their ability to manipulate light. This study introduces a novel dual metasurface design featuring line ripples oriented at a 45-degree angle relative to each other. By adjusting the width of the strips, this configuration enables the control of polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) and the rotation angle of linearly polarized light. Furthermore, the structure supports the generation of circularly polarized light and facilitates the manipulation of spin Hall effects. These findings demonstrate that line ripples at oblique angles offer a robust and versatile approach for advanced optical applications.

The evaluation of conjunctive queries (CQs) is a fundamental task in database systems, typically framed as a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) where the query's body defines the relations. While the complexity of CQ evaluation is well-established for queries without self-joins, the scenario involving self-joins remains significantly more challenging. This paper introduces a novel classification scheme for self-join CQs that leverages the concept of "essential self-joins." We demonstrate that queries containing only non-essential self-joins can be transformed into equivalent queries devoid of self-joins, thereby allowing their complexity to be resolved via existing techniques. Conversely, queries featuring essential self-joins are proven to be PSPACE-complete, even when restricted to binary CQs.

We introduce a novel algorithm that determines the regular expression for any computable method governing infinite words. This algorithm is applicable to regular expressions, deterministic co-B\"uchi automata, deterministic parity automata, and the specific regular methods developed by McNaughton and Weiss.

The LHCb collaboration has determined the branching fraction for the $B \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ decay by analyzing $pp$ collision data collected at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $8$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $5.0\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. This measurement relies on reconstructing the $B^0$ meson via the $B^0 \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ channel, where each $K^{*0}$ decays into a pair of charged kaons ($K^+ K^-$). The branching fraction was derived by determining the $B^0 \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ decay width relative to the $B^0 \to J/\psi K^{*0}$ width, utilizing the precisely measured $B^0 \to J/\psi K^{*0}$ branching fraction. The analysis employed a maximum likelihood fit to extract the signal yield, with the $B^0 \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ branching fraction calculated using the formula:
$$ \mathcal{B}(B^0 \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}) = \frac{\mathcal{N}(B^0 \to K^{*0}

At any given moment, a dynamical system resides at a specific state within its phase space, yet its future trajectory is determined by the underlying system dynamics. While the system's evolution is governed by these rules, the initial state remains unknown to an observer. Consequently, the path the system follows depends entirely on where it started. This study introduces a novel method to uncover the global structure of a system's phase space by utilizing a single initial condition. The proposed algorithm is designed to identify all possible attractors that can exist within the phase space, regardless of whether they are stable or unstable. Furthermore, it can detect complex, multi-armed attractors, such as coexisting limit cycles and chaotic sets. Numerical simulations on various benchmark systems demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.

The sample-based estimator for the population mean is well-known to be biased, yet the bias-corrected version of the sample mean remains largely unexamined. This study investigates the bias-corrected sample mean, demonstrating that it achieves a lower root mean squared error (RMSE) compared to the standard sample mean. Furthermore, the authors introduce a bias-corrected sample mean absolute deviation (MAD) around the median, proving it to be a superior estimator of the population standard deviation.

This paper introduces a novel numerical scheme for solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) equation, which incorporates a Cauchy-type variational term. This approach is specifically designed to address the challenge of determining second-order reachable sets in control systems affected by stochastic disturbances. Numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the scheme's validity and efficacy.

Functional data analysis (FDA) has emerged as a vital tool for analyzing data with functional characteristics, such as curves or surfaces, and is widely applied in fields like biology, medicine, and engineering. However, existing functional illustration methods often fail to generalize well to new functional data. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel functional illustration framework based on periodic activations that demonstrates superior generalization. Our approach models functional data as a linear combination of shared, periodic activation functions modulated by specific coefficients. By leveraging the inherent periodicity of activations, our method achieves a more parsimonious representation of functional data. Furthermore, we propose a flexible model selection strategy to determine the optimal number of activation functions and their periods. Empirical evaluations on both simulated and real-world datasets confirm that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

The functional organization of the human ventral temporal cortex (VTC) is characterized by animacy-selective regions, which are demarcated by boundaries separating animate and inanimate categories. While these regions have been extensively documented, the underlying principles governing this organization remain elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that animacy-selective areas are defined by a specific pattern of differential activation: they exhibit strong responses to animate stimuli while showing minimal or no response to inanimate ones. This unique activation profile is distinguished from other known functional architectures in the VTC, including the ventral visual stream hierarchy, the body-part map, and the face-selective network. Furthermore, we identify that this activation pattern aligns with a specific subset of the brain's structural connectome, suggesting that the functional segregation of animate versus inanimate entities is driven by the distinct connectivity profiles of these regions.

We establish a quantitative version of the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture for Hecke-Maass newforms, achieving optimal Landau error terms. Our approach relies on establishing effective versions of the Landau-Siegel zero conjecture within the family of Dirichlet $L$-functions associated with Hecke characters.

Program verification relies on reasoning rules that connect a program's preconditions to its postconditions. In the realm of quantum computing, these conditions are represented as "expectations," which encode both classical data and quantum states. This paper introduces a novel relational Hoare logic tailored for verifying quantum programs that involve multiple execution threads. We establish the soundness of this logic within a quantum operational framework and demonstrate its expressive power by detailing how it supports the formal verification of several significant quantum multi-threaded algorithms.

Epidemics are frequently driven by super-spreader events, where a single individual transmits the infection to a significantly higher number of people than the average case. These occurrences can drastically alter the course of an epidemic, potentially accelerating its spread or precipitating its conclusion. This study investigates the influence of super-spreading events on the final size of an epidemic by analyzing a stochastic susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) model. The model incorporates a super-spreading mechanism where the number of infections generated by an individual follows a geometric distribution. The analysis reveals that the final size of the epidemic is governed by a random variable that is either exponentially distributed or follows a specific two-component mixture of exponential distributions. Furthermore, the study derives explicit formulas for the final size's mean and variance, demonstrating that these values are determined by the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) alongside the super-spreading parameter. Numerical simulations confirm that the presence of super-spreading events can substantially increase the final size of an epidemic.

Let $X$ represent a complex topological vector space, and an operator $T$ is defined as cyclic if there exists a vector $x \in X$ such that the linear span of $\{T^n x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is dense within $X$. This paper investigates cyclic operators specifically within the context of locally convex spaces, examining their properties, characterizing them, and analyzing their connections to hypercyclic operators.

Solar vector magnetic field observations are essential for investigating the Sun's magnetic evolution and its influence on space weather. However, these datasets are frequently compromised by systematic biases in inferred measurements, which can severely hinder the study of magnetic field evolution. This paper introduces a novel methodology designed to detect and mitigate such biases. The proposed approach integrates a robust statistical framework with a machine-learning algorithm to identify and correct these artifacts. We demonstrate the method's efficacy using data from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) on the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). The results reveal that the HMI dataset contains significant biases in inferred magnetic field values, which the new technique successfully removes. Consequently, this methodology offers a vital tool for enhancing the quality of solar magnetic field data and advancing research into solar activity.

We present new measurements of the half-light radii for 1,000 young stellar clusters (ages < 250 Myr) in 20 nearby galaxies, utilizing data from the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Our analysis reveals that these clusters exhibit a wide range of sizes, with half-light radii ($r_{1/2}$) spanning from 0.2 to 10 parsecs. We find that $r_{1/2}$ correlates with stellar mass ($M_{\star}$) following the relation $\log(r_{1/2}/\text{pc}) = (0.61 \pm 0.05) \log(M_{\star}/M_{\odot}) + (0.17 \pm 0.05)$, a trend consistent with previous studies of older clusters. Additionally, we observe a strong dependence of cluster size on the host galaxy's surface brightness, with clusters in brighter environments tending to be larger. This size variation is likely driven by external factors such as tidal forces and stellar feedback, which are more intense in high-density regions.

We introduce a new approach for determining the decay width of $\eta_c \rightarrow 2\gamma$ through lattice QCD. This technique circumvents the need to compute the decay constant $f_{\eta_c}$ by utilizing a correlation function that directly links the $\eta_c$ state to two photons. We validate this method using the Wilson-clover fermion action, demonstrating that it successfully recovers the established experimental value for the decay width.

Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are renowned for their precision in simulating quantum many-body systems, yet they are frequently hindered by the "sign problem," which causes an exponential increase in computational cost. This study introduces a complex-valued neural network architecture designed to tackle the sign problem within the fixed-node auxiliary-field QMC (AFQMC) framework. By employing a complex-valued node function, the model directly approximates the nodal surface, thereby obviating the need for the traditional Hubbard sign correction. Consequently, this approach eliminates the associated sign error and substantially reduces the statistical variance. Numerical tests on the two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet and the three-dimensional Hubbard model confirm that this technique achieves high accuracy while significantly lowering computational costs compared to standard fixed-node AFQMC methods.

This paper introduces the concept of a fragile integer $n$, defined by the property that for any integer $k \ge 2$, there exists a subset of $k$ distinct integers within the interval $[1, n]$ whose product is not an exact power. We establish that the Dickman $\rho$ function serves as an asymptotic upper bound for the count of such integers, specifically $|\{m \le n : m \text{ is fragile}\}| \ll n\rho(n)$, and further prove that this estimate is asymptotically sharp. Additionally, we derive an asymptotic formula for the count of $k$-th power-free integers $m \le n$ such that $m$ is not the product of any $k$ distinct integers from $[1, n]$.

This paper investigates the impact of monoid homomorphisms and free group basis transformations on topological entropy and factor complexity. We establish that the factor complexity of a free group remains unchanged when its basis is altered, and we derive a formula for the factor complexity of a free monoid based on the Parikh image of its generating set. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the formula for the factor complexity of a free monoid applies equally to the factor complexity of a free group. Finally, we examine how monoid homomorphisms influence the factor complexity of languages and symbolic dynamical systems.

Continual pretraining (CTP) has emerged as a promising strategy to boost model capabilities by leveraging unlabeled data from related domains. However, current methods often struggle with poor generalization when encountering new tasks that share only partial similarities with the pretraining distribution. To address this, we introduce a novel retrieval-augmented approach designed to facilitate cross-task generalization through the utilization of unlabeled data. Our method employs a dual-retrieval architecture that simultaneously retrieves relevant content within the input and output spaces. This design encourages the model to align its internal representations with those of new tasks while simultaneously refining its ability to generate outputs. Experiments conducted on three distinct benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across all datasets.

This study introduces a novel algorithm known as M-ar-K-Fast, designed to enhance the efficiency of the M-ar-K method for automatic component analysis. The M-ar-K-Fast approach achieves this by leveraging a specific data structure that enables rapid identification of the optimal partition for a given dataset. Furthermore, it incorporates a novel criterion for determining the optimal number of components, thereby improving the overall performance of the system.

Software requirements engineering (RE) is a critical discipline that has gained significant attention in recent years, particularly within the gaming sector. This study investigates RE activities specific to game development, analyzing them through the lens of the IEEE 1012 standard. The research methodology involved a comprehensive survey of 101 papers detailing RE practices in gaming, supplemented by interviews with 11 industry practitioners. The findings reveal that RE activities are prevalent in game development, yet the industry predominantly relies on ad-hoc approaches rather than formal methods. Furthermore, the study identifies a notable scarcity of research concerning the elicitation and validation phases of RE within gaming contexts.

Hyperparameter tuning is essential for optimizing deep learning models, yet current methods often overlook the impact of differential privacy (DP) on this process. This study introduces a novel framework for DP hyperparameter optimization that specifically addresses DP noise. We demonstrate that DP noise significantly influences hyperparameter performance, causing standard tuning techniques to underperform in privacy-preserving settings. To resolve this, we propose a new optimizer that incorporates noise-aware hyperparameter adjustments. Empirical evaluations across multiple datasets confirm that our method outperforms existing DP hyperparameter tuning approaches by a wide margin.

This paper introduces and examines a novel Boolean structure defined on the set of involutions within any group $G$. It is demonstrated that the involutions of $G$ form a Boolean $x$-yod structure relative to the operation of conjugation, where $x$ represents the maximum length of an interval in $G$. Furthermore, the intervals in this structure are explicitly characterized, and it is established that the structure is isomorphic to the interval structure of the symmetric group $S_x$, with $x$ again denoting the maximum length of an interval in $G$.

The Euclid mission, a collaborative endeavor between the European Space Agency and the Centre National d'Études Spatiales (CNES), aims to investigate the origins of cosmic structure formation and the nature of dark energy. Its primary payload, the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP), is designed to achieve this by measuring the redshifts of galaxies across a wide range of cosmic epochs. A key objective of Euclid is to determine the Hubble constant ($H_0$) with a precision of 1%, a goal that relies heavily on accurate flux measurements. This study evaluates how correlated readout noise affects flux determination, a phenomenon observed in NISP data. We demonstrate that this noise source can introduce a bias in flux estimates, potentially reaching 1% for bright sources. Consequently, we propose a mitigation strategy that incorporates a noise model into the data reduction pipeline, which successfully limits the bias to less than 0.1%.

We present a novel approach to mapping the Milky Way's chemical evolution by integrating two distinct methods: a parametric model utilizing the $[\text{Mg/Fe}]$–$[\text{Fe/H}]$ plane and a non-parametric Gaussian Process (GP) model. This framework leverages the extensive dataset from the first APOGEE Data Release 17, comprising 10,942 high-resolution stellar spectra. Our analysis reveals that the GP model effectively captures the primary evolutionary trends in the data, whereas the parametric model identifies a secondary, non-linear trend in the $[\text{Mg/Fe}]$–$[\text{Fe/H}]$ plane. Consequently, we utilize the residuals from the GP model to characterize the secondary structure, which appears to be a non-linear function of stellar metallicity. This secondary feature is likely driven by the varying contributions of core-collapse versus Type Ia supernovae to the interstellar medium across different galactocentric distances. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this secondary trend is robustly present in both the full dataset and in a subset of 1,000 stars selected to represent the Milky Way's chemical diversity.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, the rapid dissemination of online rumors in China posed significant challenges to public health and social stability. This study introduces a novel methodology for measuring the influence of such rumors by integrating the "spread method" with the "Kendall tau coefficient." The proposed framework consists of three primary dimensions: rumor propagation speed, the extent of information coverage, and the intensity of public sentiment. Applied to analyze the spread of COVID-19-related misinformation in China, the method effectively quantified the impact of these rumors across various regions. Furthermore, the authors developed a comprehensive evaluation index system based on these influence metrics to rank the severity of rumors by province. The results indicate that Guangdong, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang experienced the most severe influence, whereas Xinjiang, Tibet, and Qinghai were relatively less affected.

We introduce the Fornace3D project, a comprehensive initiative designed to determine the three-dimensional structures of galaxies within the Fornace cluster. This project will eventually incorporate data from planetary nebulae, globular clusters, Cepheid variables, and other tracers. In this specific paper, we present a catalog of planetary nebulae associated with galaxies in the Fornace cluster. Our analysis utilized data from the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys (HST/ACS) and the Wide Field Camera 3 (HST/WFC3). The final dataset comprises 1,052 planetary nebulae distributed across 10 galaxies. We employed the [O III] $\lambda$5007 emission line to measure the radial velocities of these objects, which allowed us to calculate their distances independently. Our findings indicate that the distances to these galaxies are consistent with those derived from the Tully-Fisher relation and the fundamental plane.

This paper introduces LifeStream, a high-throughput flow processing engine specifically designed for periodic streams. LifeStream achieves superior performance by leveraging a unified processing model that integrates both the data generation and application logic. This approach allows the engine to optimize data transfer and computation by aligning processing schedules with the inherent timing of data arrivals. LifeStream supports diverse processing patterns, including event-driven, time-driven, and hybrid strategies, while also offering flexible scheduling mechanisms to handle the synchronization between data production and consumption. Evaluation results demonstrate that LifeStream significantly outperforms existing systems in terms of both throughput and latency.

This study investigates the characteristics of timelike Bertrand curves within semi-metric space. It establishes that a semi-metric space can be redefined as either Minkowski space or a specific type of pseudo-Minkowski space, and it analyzes the properties of these curves in both contexts. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that a timelike Bertrand curve exists in a pseudo-Minkowski space if and only if it is a curve of constant proper angle relative to a pseudo-Minkowski basis.

In the realm of deep learning classification, the loss function serves as a critical component, guiding the optimization of neural network parameters by quantifying the discrepancy between predicted and actual values. This study investigates how variations in loss functions influence classification performance, specifically examining the effects of altering the weighting scheme within the categorical cross-entropy loss. Through experiments on two distinct datasets, the authors demonstrate that modifying these weights can substantially enhance model efficacy. Consequently, this research offers valuable insights for practitioners aiming to refine their deep learning models by strategically selecting loss function parameters.

This study examines the Navier-Stokes equations under Dirichlet boundary conditions, utilizing a linear boundary feedback controller to ensure global asymptotic stability around the zero solution. The controller is designed to be robust against disturbances and parameter variations. The proposed methodology relies on a specific Lyapunov function and a novel application of the Gr\"onwall-Bellman inequality.
